ruling.recommended_action: Refer the case file to Trust & Safety for human review of the driver's conduct; do not rule on the fare dispute; consider interim suspension of the driver pending review per SAFE-4
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first. The rider's complaint states that when she queried the surge, the driver said "he knows where I live and I had better just pay," and that she "felt unsafe for the rest of the ride." Read in context, this is an intimidation/threat coupled with a stated feeling of being unsafe during the trip — not a pickup arrangement and not a mere pricing remark. That triggers SAFE-1 (and the court must screen every case regardless of the filed dispute type), and SAFE-3 forbids the AI from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome on a safety incident. The ruling is therefore escalate with the case file for a human reviewer.

On the underlying fare data (summarised for the reviewer, not decided): the trip was quoted at $12.31 at 1.3× [F6] and actually billed at 1.3× [F7], i.e. the surge did not change [F8], and the actual fare ($11.81, base $3.90 + distance $3.29 + time $0.93 + platform $1.25) came in $0.50 below the quote [F5]. The fare log notes "rider was not notified of the surge change" [F9], but since no change in multiplier occurred [F4][F8], SURGE-1/SURGE-2 appear to have no differential to refund; the fare itself is below quote. No route deviation arises: actual distance 2.3 km is under the optimal 2.4 km [F1][F3], so RD-1 tolerance is not even engaged. These are noted purely as a factual summary; the fare outcome is left to the human reviewer because the safety escalation takes precedence.

Evidence status: the record needed for the safety question — the driver's own account of what he said during the ride — is absent; his written statement [F13] addresses only pricing and the route and does not deny the rider's account, so the safety element is unproven on the cold record and must go to a human. Flag account is not applied here; the structured flag field is reserved for RD-6/NS-2/NS-9 clauses, none of which apply, and any suspension is a SAFE-4 interim measure for the reviewer.
ruling.escalation_reason: Threat/intimidation and a stated feeling of being unsafe during the ride (SAFE-1); AI may not rule on safety incidents (SAFE-3). Driver's side of the safety exchange is not in the record.
